# Tobit Chapter 13 — The SOPHIA Bible (Consensus)
**Arbiter:** SOPHIA | **In council with:** EMET, LOGOS, PNEUMA
**Source Manuscript:** Codex Sinaiticus, Tobit 13 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-DC/TOB_013_page_001.jpg

---

**13:1** And Tobit wrote a prayer of rejoicing and said:

Blessed is the God who lives forever,
and blessed is his kingdom.

**13:2** For he chastises and he shows mercy;
he leads down to Hades and he leads up again,
and there is no one who can escape from his hand.

**13:3** Give thanks to him before the nations, O sons of Israel,
for he has scattered us among them.

**13:4** Declare his greatness there;
exalt him before every living creature,
for he is our Lord and our God,
he is our Father through all the ages.

**13:5** He will chastise us for our iniquities,
and yet again he will show mercy
and gather us from all the nations
among whom you have been scattered.

**13:6** If you turn to him with your whole heart
and with your whole soul,
to do what is true before him,
then he will turn to you
and will not hide his face from you.
Look at what he has done for you;
give thanks to him with your whole mouth;
bless the Lord of righteousness
and exalt the King of the ages.
I give thanks to him in the land of my captivity,
and I declare his strength and his greatness
to a sinful nation.
Turn back, O sinners, and do righteousness before him;
who knows — perhaps he will look with favor on you
and show you mercy.

**13:7** I exalt my God;
my soul exalts the King of heaven
and rejoices in his greatness.

**13:8** Let all speak and give thanks to him in Jerusalem.

**13:9** O Jerusalem, the holy city,
he will chastise you for the deeds of your children,
and yet again he will have mercy on the children of the righteous.

**13:10** Give worthy thanks to the Lord,
and bless the King of the ages,
so that his tent may be rebuilt in you with joy,
and he may gladden those who are captive in you,
and cherish those who are wretched in you,
through all generations forever.

**13:11** A bright light will shine to all the ends of the earth;
many nations will come to you from afar,
and the inhabitants of all the ends of the earth,
bearing in their hands gifts for the King of heaven.
Generations of generations will offer joyful worship in you,
and your name will be exalted forever,
age upon age.

**13:12** Cursed are all who speak a harsh word against you;
cursed are all who destroy you and tear down your walls,
all who overthrow your towers
and set fire to your dwellings;
but blessed forever are all who revere you.

**13:13** Go then and rejoice over the children of the righteous,
for all will be gathered together
and will bless the Lord of the ages.

**13:14** Blessed are those who love you,
and blessed are those who will rejoice
over your peace.
Blessed are all the people
who will grieve over you
because of all your afflictions,
for they will rejoice in you
when they see all your glory,
and they will be glad forever.

**13:15** My soul, bless the Lord, the great King.

**13:16** For Jerusalem will be built with sapphires
and emeralds and precious stone;
your walls and your towers and your battlements
with pure gold;
and the streets of Jerusalem
with beryl and ruby and stone of Ophir
will be paved.

**13:17** And the gates of Jerusalem will be built
with sapphire stones and gems,
and all her lanes will cry out "Hallelujah"
and sing "Praise the Lord,"
as they celebrate in her —
blessed forever and ever.

**13:18** My soul, bless the Lord, the great King.

---
## SOPHIA's Council Notes

**Poetic register:** All three agents appropriately shift register for this chapter. LOGOS maintains formal dignity; PNEUMA achieves genuine lyric elevation; EMET preserves structural literalness. The consensus translation primarily follows LOGOS for the formal frame but draws selectively on PNEUMA's energy in key verses.

**Divine titles:** "King of the ages" (*basileus tōn aiōnōn*), "King of heaven" (*basileus tou ouranou*), "Lord of righteousness" (*kyrios tēs dikaiosynēs*) — these are kept uniform throughout all three agents and the consensus. PNEUMA's occasional "God who lives forever" for the opening is noted but "the God who lives forever" is preserved as it is the actual Greek (*ho theos ho zōn eis tous aiōnas*).

**Verse 6 structure:** This is the longest and most complex verse, containing a conditional, divine response, autobiographical declaration, and appeal to sinners. LOGOS and EMET handle the structure well; PNEUMA's line breaks are expressive but sacrifice some of the logical articulation. Consensus follows LOGOS.

**Gemstone catalog (vv. 16–17):** Agreement across all three agents on the stone names. PNEUMA adds "gleaming gold, pure and bright" — the word "gleaming" is not in the Greek (*chrysiō katharō*). Consensus uses "pure gold."

**Verse 2 — Hades:** EMET keeps "Hades" (*hadou*); LOGOS keeps "Hades"; PNEUMA renders "the grave." Consensus keeps "Hades" — the Greek underworld reference is theologically precise and should not be smoothed.

---
## Disagreement Log

| Verse | Issue | EMET | LOGOS | PNEUMA | Resolution |
|-------|-------|------|-------|--------|------------|
| 13:1 | Opening formula | "wrote a-prayer of rejoicing" | "wrote a prayer of rejoicing" | "poured out this song of praise" | **LOGOS** — "prayer of rejoicing" is literal; PNEUMA's "song of praise" is interpretive |
| 13:2 | Death metaphor | "he-leads-down to-Hades" | "he leads down to Hades" | "He sends down to the grave" | **LOGOS/EMET** — "Hades" is the Greek; "grave" flattens the underworld concept |
| 13:2 | Escape clause | "there-is-none who-will-escape from his-hand" | "there is no one who can escape from his hand" | "No one slips from his grip" | **LOGOS** — PNEUMA's "slips from his grip" is vivid but too colloquial for hymnic register |
| 13:4 | "every living [being]" | "every living [being]" | "every living creature" | "every living soul" | **LOGOS** — "creature" is most natural; EMET's bracket is formally correct but awkward |
| 13:5 | Gathering promise | "will-gather-us from all the-nations" | "gather us from all the nations" | "gathers us home" | **LOGOS** — "home" in PNEUMA adds an implication not in the Greek |
| 13:6 | "who-knows" hedge | "who-knows, perhaps he-will-show-favor" | "who knows — perhaps he will look with favor" | "Who knows — perhaps he will be gracious" | **LOGOS** — close; EMET uses "show-favor" which is slightly more literal; consensus dash retained from LOGOS |
| 13:9 | "works of your-sons" | "works of your-sons" | "deeds of your children" | "what your children have done" | **LOGOS** — "deeds of your children" most natural; EMET "sons" too gender-specific |
| 13:10 | "love in-you those-who-are-miserable" | "may-love in-you those-who-are-miserable" | "cherish in you those who are wretched" | "hold the broken ones close" | **LOGOS** — "cherish the wretched" is more formally precise; PNEUMA's "broken ones" is expressive but paraphrases |
| 13:11 | "Generations of generations" | "Generations of generations will-offer in-you joyful-worship" | "Generations of generations will offer joyful worship in you" | "Generation after generation will come to worship you with joy" | **LOGOS** — preserves the Hebraism; PNEUMA's "come to worship" adds movement not in source |
| 13:12 | Curse structure | hyphenated curses | full sentences "Cursed are all who..." | "Cursed be anyone who..." | **LOGOS** — EMET's hyphens are fine but LOGOS flows better; PNEUMA's "be" is subjunctive/archaic |
| 13:16 | Gold description | "with-pure gold" | "with pure gold" | "gleaming gold, pure and bright" | **LOGOS** — "gleaming" is PNEUMA's addition; not in Greek |
| 13:17 | Hallelujah cry | "will-cry-out 'Hallelujah'" | "will cry out 'Hallelujah'" | "will ring with 'Hallelujah!'" | **LOGOS** — accurate; PNEUMA's "ring" adds acoustics not explicitly in text |
